name: Michael J. Cavanagh

career.title: Various roles, incl. CFO of the Consumer Group for Europe, Middle East and Africa
Head of Strategy and Planning, Treasurer, then CEO/COO of Middle Market Banking
CEO of Treasury & Securities Services, then Co-CEO of the Corporate & Investment Bank (2012-2014)
Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

background_rationale: Spent two decades in banking finance and strategy roles, including six years as JPMorgan Chase's CFO, before joining Comcast as CFO in 2015.

notable.summary: As co-CEO-designate, Cavanagh explained Comcast's decision not to pursue Warner Bros. Discovery further after Netflix won the bidding, saying the company was not interested in stressing its balance sheet.
Took office as co-CEO and joined Comcast's board in the same week the company completed the spin-off of its cable networks into Versant Media Group.
Comcast announced it would separate into two public companies within about a year, with Cavanagh named to become CEO of the spun-off NBCUniversal, including Sky.

On the second-quarter earnings call, Cavanagh said the goal was to complete the separation in about a year with strong investment-grade profiles for both companies, as Peacock reported its first profitable quarter.

personal_story.hook: He pumped gas as a teenager and worked construction summers to get through Yale; now Mike Cavanagh co-runs Comcast.
personal_story.summary: Cavanagh grew up in a middle-class Irish-Catholic family on Long Island and pumped gas at a filling station before college. At Yale he rowed crew and worked summer construction jobs to cover expenses, graduating in 1988 with a history degree, then earned a law degree from the University of Chicago in 1993. He went into banking instead of law, became a protege of Jamie Dimon, and followed him to Bank One and JPMorgan Chase, where he served as CFO through the 2008 financial crisis. After a brief stint at Carlyle, he joined Comcast as CFO in 2015, became its first president from outside the Roberts family in 2022, and co-CEO in 2026.
